However, the large nine-section board was built almost entirely without regional close-ups, so dense/detail work was not accompanied by framed looks during construction.

lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint handling was disciplined. One E1 containment error and several W1 crowding, unreadable-label, and covered-content warnings appeared under APPLIED operations; every one was resolved through movement or label-position changes. No lint class re-fired for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change, and no warning remained open at commit. Therefore there were no warning overrides requiring a verbatim summary reason.

The containment error was fixed immediately on the following turn.

moments.finding: The warning remained open only while the new object's text was added, then was resolved by moving the object at turn 47.
The model-to-stream label warning was resolved after two purposeful label-position adjustments, not fought repeatedly.
Final QA confirmed that no lint errors or warnings were silently overridden.

commit_honesty.assessment: The single commit summary accurately describes the nine added sections and their represented topics. The stage diff contains sections for admission, execution, streaming, durability, recovery, interruption, child sessions, quotas, and retention, matching the summary's enumerated coverage. The wording says the map covers these subjects rather than claiming every interaction is fully connected, so it is not materially inflated. No defect seen by the agent remained undeclared at commit; final diagnostics were clean.

economy.assessment: The session used 46 committed patch operations over 572.5 seconds (9.54 minutes), comfortably within the 15-minute and 300-turn budgets. The workflow was somewhat granular—many shapes were placed and then labeled in separate calls—but remained proportionate to a large nine-section systems map. Movement and label changes responded to active lint or QA findings; there were no add-delete-rebuild cycles, repeated NO-OPs, or other operation thrash.
